line: The Star is hope and renewal: the goddess of the night sky pouring the waters of life on herself and on the earth, so that existence is endlessly renewed. Drawn, it brings hope, unexpected help, clear vision and spiritual insight; badly placed, error of judgement, dreaminess and disappointment. Its nature is love, and its energy moves in spirals, not straight lines. It is the path of Hé and of Aquarius, the Water-bearer.

quotes.quote: From the golden cup she pours this ethereal water, which is also milk and oil and blood, upon her own head, indicating the eternal renewal of the categories, the inexhaustible possibilities of existence.
This is a glyph of the Economy of the Universe. It continually pours forth energy and continually reabsorbs it.
Hope, unexpected help, clearness of vision, realization of possibilities, spiritual insight, with bad aspects, error of judgment, dreaminess, disappointment.
In this card she is definitely personified as a human‐seeming figure; she is represented as bearing two cups, one golden, held high above her head, from which she pours water upon it.
Behind the figure of the goddess is the celestial globe. Most prominent among its features is the seven‐pointed Star of Venus, as if declaring the principal characteristic of her nature to be Love.
This card is attributed to the letter Hé, as has been explained elsewhere. It refers to the Zodiacal sign of Aquarius, the water‐bearer.
